questions.text: Describe a data pipeline you built or maintained. How did you make sure it loaded the right data every time?

follow_up_suggestions.text: How did the pipeline handle late or duplicate records?
How did you know when something went wrong?

scoring_rubric.2: Describes loading steps without correctness checks
scoring_rubric.3: Uses idempotent loads, retries and basic checks
scoring_rubric.4: Handles late and duplicate data and alerts on failures
scoring_rubric.5: Also explains backfills, data contracts and recovery procedures

questions.text: How do you model data in a warehouse so that analysts can answer new questions without rebuilding everything?

follow_up_suggestions.text: What is the difference between your fact and dimension tables in practice?
How do you handle a field whose definition changes over time?

scoring_rubric.2: Stores raw data only, with no structure
scoring_rubric.3: Uses a clear star or layered model with documentation
scoring_rubric.4: Handles slowly changing dimensions and naming conventions
scoring_rubric.5: Also designs for governance, reuse and a clear data ownership model

questions.text: A business dashboard shows numbers that do not match the finance report. How do you find out why?

follow_up_suggestions.text: Which step of the pipeline would you check first, and how?
How do you agree the correct number with the finance team?

scoring_rubric.2: Compares totals without tracing the cause
scoring_rubric.3: Traces the numbers back through each transformation step
scoring_rubric.4: Finds the definition or filter difference and documents it
scoring_rubric.5: Also adds reconciliation tests to prevent the same gap returning

questions.text: How do you test data quality in a pipeline? Give an example of a check that caught a real problem.

follow_up_suggestions.text: Which tests are automatic, and which need a person to look?
What happens in the pipeline when a check fails?

scoring_rubric.3: Uses null, range and uniqueness checks with alerts
scoring_rubric.4: Adds freshness checks and blocks bad data from publishing
scoring_rubric.5: Also tracks quality trends and assigns owners to each check

questions.text: When would you choose batch processing over streaming, and how would you explain that choice to a product team?

follow_up_suggestions.text: What latency does the product team actually need?
What does streaming cost in operations compared with batch?

scoring_rubric.3: Matches latency needs and operating cost to the choice
scoring_rubric.4: Explains failure handling and complexity differences clearly
scoring_rubric.5: Also proposes a phased path and measures whether the choice met the need
